output.summary: The rise in median ED arrival-to-departure time for admitted patients (4.1 h to 7.3 h) is almost entirely boarding: boarding rose about 3.0 h of the 3.2 h increase, while ED work-up time moved only 0.2 h. Boarding jumped in March 2026, when the hospitalist rounding change shifted medical-ward discharges later; surgical wards, which were not changed, are unaffected. The 4 West huddle pilot, with rotation-assigned days and an unaffected comparison ward, cut boarding from 4.6 h to 2.3 h. Nurse staffing hours, visit volume, acuity and bed capacity did not worsen, so understaffing is contradicted as the main cause. The travel-nurse contract funded by deferring case managers, and pausing the huddle, are harmful. Extending the huddle is preferred. Key gaps: hospitalist census, the front-end APP change, and EVS turnaround data.
